claimUnderTest.summary: would-affect-edge is a 1:1 immutable evt_-to-subject edge, not a multi-target zoning-impact relation. ./temporal exports are dormant in serving repos. Obligation atom type (entity_type obligation) is dormant with zero atoms rows. Forward consequence is not present-tense.

exportPaths.obligation: root barrel only (src/obligation.ts); NO ./obligation subpath in package.json exports

wouldAffectEdge.quotedDefinition: Structural edge from an event node to a subject node. sourceNodeId MUST carry the evt_ prefix. targetSubjectId carries a subject prefix (parcel_, jurisdiction_, etc.). effectiveDate is the ISO 8601 calendar date the event takes effect. immutable: true — structural, never updated after deposit; supersession is via a new edge deposit.
wouldAffectEdge.misreadRisk: Name suggests 'which parcels would an amendment affect' (1:N query relation). Contract is one evt_ node linked to one subject node per edge record. Multi-subject coverage requires N edge deposits, not one multi-target edge.

surfaces.name: AnticipatoryAtom
surfaces.quotedDefinition: An anticipatory atom in the event family. valid_from MAY be in the future. claim_type must match anticipatory.<kind>. confidence.basis must be asserted on new deposits.
surfaces.note: Not registered as atoms.entity_type; claim_type vocabulary on event-family payloads.

surfaces.name: interval-query helpers
surfaces.quotedDefinition: Current-state queries that filter valid_from <= now silently exclude anticipatory atoms whose valid_from is in the future. Helpers make that exclusion explicit and offer opt-in to surface anticipatory atoms.
